patch_description: The current pair_polish only tries pure axial separation of the closest pair and axial contraction of the diameter pair. When a third neighbor sits along the pair axis, axial moves can be blocked, and the polish stalls. Following the recommendation, I add tangential candidate moves: when separating the closest pair, both points are also displaced with a tangential component perpendicular to the pair direction (and to the local z-axis of the pair, giving a well-defined tangent plane), at 0.3·step magnitude. This generates extra candidates per step size that let the pair "slide around" nearby obstacles at the same step scale, which can push the exact ratio past what axial moves achieve. I also apply a symmetric tangential variant for contracting the diameter pair. All candidates are accepted only on strict exact-ratio improvement, so the procedure can never degrade the result. This is a cheap change to the existing polish loop and should not increase runtime materially since it replaces unused improvement potential within the same rounds budget.
